problem:
The joint probability distribution $f(x,y)$ of the discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given below. 

| $f$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=2$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $X=1$ | $0.1$ | $0.15$ |
| $X=2$ | $0.3$ | $0.45$ |

Which of the following statements are true?

- $P(X=1,Y=2)=P(X=1)\cdot P(Y=2)$
- $P(X=x,Y=y)=P(X=x)\cdot P(Y=y)$ for all possible $x$ and $y$
- $X$ and $Y$ are independent

feedback.worked_solution:
Two discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ with joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ are independent if and only if 

$$
f(x,y)={f}_{X}(x)\cdot {f}_{Y}(y)
$$

 

for all possible values $x$ and $y,$ where ${f}_{X}(x)$ and ${f}_{Y}(y)$ are the marginal probability mass functions for $X$ and $Y,$ respectively.

Therefore, since our discrete random variables are independent, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(6,5) & ={f}_{X}(6)\cdot {f}_{Y}(5) \\  & =0.1\cdot 0.25 \\  & =0.025.\end{aligned}
$$
